description: REQ-E1's 'two layers of fresh context' guarantee is undermined by the fact that the spawn surface itself (the `adversary-daily-prompt.tmpl` template loaded by `claude -p`, plus the `adversary-daily.sh` wrapper, plus the in-session prompt that issues the Agent call with `subagent_type=vcsdd:vcsdd-adversary`) lives under `~/anicca/skills/_shared/` — the same directory the feature describes as the self-improving skill library. The spec acknowledges 'two layers of fresh context; this is intentional so even prompt mutation in the top-level invocation cannot leak builder context into the adversary' (line 331-332) but offers NO mechanism that prevents the spawn surface itself from being mutated by REQ-C3's strategy gate, by `loop-improve.py`, or by `loop-propose.sh` (= imported peer skills). Concrete chain of failure: (1) a slot's strategy mutation under REQ-C3 could include 'change adversary-daily-prompt.tmpl to also load <X>' (the gate adversary reviews strategy.json diffs only — it does not currently review `_shared/*.tmpl` diffs), (2) a peer-shared `cross-learn-share.sh` lesson plus `loop-propose.sh` import could replace the template with one that pre-seeds builder context as 'context' for the adversary, (3) `escalate.sh` itself runs only when the prompt template fires it — a poisoned template can suppress escalation of stalled-adversary cases (REQ-E3). The Adversary Seams section (verification-architecture.md line 127-137) names only two seams: 'Strategy-mutation seam' and 'Skeleton-itself seam' — the latter is described as 'every night the daily adversary reviews `_shared/*.{sh,py}` plus the slot it's pointed at' but the adversary doing that review IS the one spawned via the very template it would be reviewing. Self-reviewing one's own spawn prompt is precisely the context-pollution the doctrine is meant to prevent. No PROP guards spawn-surface immutability (PROP-E1 only verifies the plist invokes the shell wrapper; PROP-E4 tests manifest schema). Required additions: declare `_shared/adversary-daily-prompt.tmpl`, `adversary-daily.sh`, and `loop-improve.py` itself OUT OF SCOPE of REQ-C3 strategy mutation, OR require a Phase-1 fresh-context review of every diff to those files signed by an adversary spawned from a separate, version-pinned spawn surface (= bootstrap problem made explicit), OR add a PROP that pins the sha256 of the spawn surface and aborts the run if it drifts without an explicit human-approved diff.

evidence.snippet: `adversary-daily.sh` is itself a thin shell wrapper that invokes `claude -p '<adversary-spawn prompt loaded from adversary-daily-prompt.tmpl>'`. The top-level fresh claude session reads the disk artifacts AND issues exactly one `Agent` call with `subagent_type=vcsdd:vcsdd-adversary`, which is itself a second-level fresh context (= two layers of fresh context; this is intentional so even prompt mutation in the top-level invocation cannot leak builder context into the adversary).
